import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.feature_selection import mutual_info_classif
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

MAX_DRIVERS = 4

def design(feats):
    # Filter out near-duplicates based on correlation
    corr_pairs = []
    for i, fid1 in enumerate(feats.ids):
        for j, fid2 in enumerate(feats.ids[i+1:], i+1):
            if abs(np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, i], feats.x[:, j])[0,1]) >= 0.6:
                corr_pairs.append((fid1, fid2))
    
    # Remove near-duplicates, keeping first occurrence
    unique_ids = set()
    kept_ids = []
    for fid in feats.ids:
        if any(fid in pair for pair in corr_pairs):
            # Check if any correlated feature was already added
            if not any(fid in pair and any(p in kept_ids for p in pair) for pair in corr_pairs):
                kept_ids.append(fid)
        else:
            kept_ids.append(fid)
    
    # Remove duplicates while preserving order
    seen = set()
    filtered_ids = []
    for fid in kept_ids:
        if fid not in seen:
            seen.add(fid)
            filtered_ids.append(fid)
    
    # Calculate effect sizes for remaining features
    effects = []
    for fid in filtered_ids:
        idx = feats.column(fid)
        y1_mean = np.mean(feats.x[feats.y == 1, idx])
        y0_mean = np.mean(feats.x[feats.y == 0, idx])
        effect_size = abs(y1_mean - y0_mean)
        effects.append((fid, effect_size))
    
    # Sort by effect size (descending)
    effects.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
    
    # Select top features as drivers (at most MAX_DRIVERS)
    drivers = [fid for fid, _ in effects[:MAX_DRIVERS]]
    
    # Use all features that are not near-duplicates
    columns = tuple(filtered_ids)
    
    # Look for product terms between highly correlated pairs
    products = []
    for fid1, fid2 in corr_pairs:
        if fid1 in filtered_ids and fid2 in filtered_ids:
            products.append((fid1, fid2))
    
    # Build weighted score using top features
    loadings = {}
    for fid, _ in effects[:MAX_DRIVERS]:
        idx = feats.column(fid)
        # Weight by effect size
        y1_mean = np.mean(feats.x[feats.y == 1, idx])
        y0_mean = np.mean(feats.x[feats.y == 0, idx])
        loadings[fid] = abs(y1_mean - y0_mean)
    
    return Design(drivers=tuple(drivers), columns=columns, products=tuple(products), loadings=loadings)
